submission.summary: This is a 27-year-old male software developer and endurance athlete with a history of two significant medical conditions: exertional rhabdomyolysis requiring fluid resuscitation (January 2020) following a long-distance race in hot weather, and cholera (July 2020) acquired during travel to southern Mexico. His clinical trajectory shows a pattern of dehydration-related illnesses, with his most recent encounter in July 2021 for recurrent cholera after disaster relief volunteer work in rural Bangladesh, presenting with severe dehydration, profuse "rice water" diarrhea, tachycardia, and hypotension. Notably, despite having prior cholera infection, he developed a second episode, suggesting inadequate protective immunity or high re-exposure risk. The patient currently has no active problems documented, takes no medications, and has no known drug allergies. His history indicates susceptibility to both exertional heat illness and travel-related infectious diarrhea, warranting counseling on hydration strategies, heat precautions during endurance activities, and travel health measures including pre-travel vaccinations and food/water safety precautions.

Patient 2376 is a newborn male with Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) born to a mother with poorly controlled gestational diabetes mellitus and polyhydramnios. His clinical course has been complex, beginning with neonatal hypoglycemia (glucose 22 mg/dL) causing seizures and transient hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on day 1 of life. He subsequently developed bilious vomiting and was diagnosed with duodenal atresia, requiring duodenoduodenostomy repair. Persistent gastrointestinal symptoms led to a February 2020 diagnosis of Hirschsprung disease, treated with Soave pull-through procedure. By May 2020, he presented with poor feeding, failure to thrive, and easy fatigability, and was found to have complete atrioventricular septal defect requiring surgical repair. The current active problem list includes Trisomy 21, transient hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, duodenal atresia, Hirschsprung disease, and infant of diabetic mother status. He is maintained on furosemide, captopril, aspirin, and polyethylene glycol for bowel regimen. This patient demonstrates the classic multisystem involvement of Down syndrome affecting cardiac, gastrointestinal, and metabolic systems, requiring multiple surgical interventions within his first months of life.

This 78-year-old female had a progressive clinical trajectory marked by multi-system decline and catastrophic neurologic events. Her active problem list at the time of her final encounter included poorly controlled hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, multijoint osteoarthritis, non-valvular atrial fibrillation, mild cognitive impairment, neurosyphilis, aortic valve stenosis, orthostatic hypotension, history of falling, acute subdural hematoma, and cerebral amyloid angiopathy. Beginning in 2020, she developed cognitive impairment and severe aortic stenosis, followed by recurrent falls and orthostatic hypotension in 2021. In March 2022, she presented with altered mental status and was found to have an acute subdural hematoma following a recent fall. She subsequently suffered a left parietal lobar intracerebral hemorrhage in September 2022, attributed to cerebral amyloid angiopathy, presenting with aphasia and right hemiparesis. She ultimately presented on March 15, 2023, found unresponsive at home with massive right cerebral hemisphere edema, developed herniation, and died within hours despite supportive measures.
